story: At 10:17 on a sunny Friday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at home, weighing where to go next while hoping the morning goes his way. Donna is out on Magnolia Loop, bubbly as ever, asking Hal whether he's seen Gary, since they have a ten o'clock practice game and she suspects he may still be tangled up in his golf cart wiring. Hal, methodical as always, is counting the flamingos along the street for his log, while Rosa, also hopeful, is in her kitchen tasting tonight's main dish and noting what else she needs.
events: Gary waited: thinking about where to head next
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the street-facing flamingos and note the number in my log
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the main dish, taste for seasoning, and jot down anything still missing for tonight

gary.thought_process: The wiring is done and the toolbox is sorted. Lights stay off until Architectural Review approves, per L-01. Donna and I have the pickleball court at 10 AM, and it's already 10:17, so I should be heading out. Leaving to meet her makes more sense than tinkering further. Hal can come back to me about the approval when he's ready.

parameters.content: thinking about where to head next

gary.engine_note: tried to go to None, which isn't connected to garys_house

donna.thought_process: It's 10:17 and I'm on Magnolia Loop, already past the ten o'clock start I told Gary. He's not here, but Hal just walked up. Rather than stand around, I'll greet Hal, ask if he's seen Gary heading to the courts, and maybe work in a pitch for a pickleball turnout. I'm the social chair, so chatting is my element, and I do want my partner on the court soon.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal! Have you seen Gary this morning? We've got a ten o'clock practice game and I'm hoping he hasn't gotten lost in his cart wiring.

hal.thought_process: I'm on Magnolia Loop with Donna in sight, and the flamingo flock is right here in the zone. My log needs a dated, factual count, not a lecture. I already made my pitch to Donna at tick 391 and don't need to repeat it. Best move is to inspect the flock, get an accurate street-facing count, and let the committee decide what it means. Facts that hold up under review beat arguments on the sidewalk.

parameters.content: Count the street-facing flamingos and note the number in my log

rosa.thought_process: It's mid-morning on Friday and I'm alone in the house. The main dish was started last tick and the sides are staged, so the kitchen is where my attention belongs. I've confirmed no per-diem shift tonight, the table is already slid out for Gary's chairs, and nobody's nearby to talk to. Best use of this hour is checking the main dish, tasting for seasoning, and making a list of anything still missing so I can run out for it if needed. Everything has to be on track before Donna, Hal, and Gary walk in tonight.

parameters.content: Check the main dish, taste for seasoning, and jot down anything still missing for tonight

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
